The described technology relates to enhanced guided surface waveguide probes, along with associated systems and methods for launching and supporting guided electromagnetic surface waves along a lossy conducting medium, such as the Earth.

In one example, a guided surface waveguide probe includes a charge terminal positioned at an elevated height above the lossy conducting medium. The charge terminal is configured to interact electromagnetically with the medium so that, when properly excited, it can generate or support a guided surface wave that propagates along the surface of the medium rather than radiating primarily into free space.

The charge terminal may be divided into two portions: an upper terminal portion and a lower terminal portion. These two portions are electrically coupled through a variable capacitance. By adjusting the variable capacitance, the electrical characteristics of the charge terminal can be tuned. This tunability allows the probe to be adapted to changing operating conditions, such as variations in frequency, medium conductivity, atmospheric conditions, or desired propagation characteristics.

A feed network is used to couple an excitation source to the charge terminal. The excitation source supplies electrical energy to the probe, while the feed network conditions that energy before it reaches the charge terminal. In particular, the feed network provides a voltage having a selected phase delay. This phase delay is chosen to correspond to the wave tilt angle associated with the complex Brewster angle of incidence for the lossy conducting medium. Matching the phase delay to this wave tilt angle helps establish the proper electromagnetic field relationship needed to efficiently launch or maintain a guided surface wave.

A corresponding method includes positioning the charge terminal at a selected elevation above the lossy conducting medium. The upper and lower terminal portions are coupled through the variable capacitance, allowing the probe to be tuned as needed. The excitation source is then coupled to the charge terminal through the feed network. During operation, the phase delay introduced by the feed network is adjusted so that the voltage applied to the charge terminal has a phase relationship matched to the wave tilt angle required for guided surface wave propagation. This adjustment supports efficient coupling of energy into a surface-guided mode along the lossy conducting medium.

Overall, the enhanced guided surface waveguide probe provides a tunable structure for generating guided surface waves. By combining an elevated charge terminal, a variable capacitance between terminal portions, and a feed network configured to provide a phase delay matched to the complex Brewster angle condition, the system improves control over the launching and propagation of electromagnetic energy along a lossy conducting surface.
outputs.L4:
Enhanced guided surface waveguide probes and related methods are designed to efficiently launch and support guided surface waves along the surface of a lossy conducting medium, such as soil, earth, seawater, or another imperfectly conducting material. In these systems, an elevated charge terminal is positioned above the lossy conducting medium and is arranged so that electric charge may be distributed in a controlled manner relative to the surface. The elevated charge terminal may include an upper terminal portion and a lower terminal portion, which are electrically related but separated in a way that permits a controllable or adjustable capacitance between them.

A feed network is coupled to the elevated charge terminal and is configured to deliver electrical energy to the terminal structure. The feed network may include one or more inductive, capacitive, or impedance-transforming elements that are adjusted to establish a desired voltage and current relationship at the probe. In particular, the feed network and the variable capacitance between the upper and lower terminal portions are tuned so that the electromagnetic fields produced by the probe correspond to the wave tilt angle associated with the complex Brewster angle of the lossy conducting medium.

By matching the field structure generated by the probe to the propagation characteristics of the medium, the probe can excite a guided surface wave in a phase-matched manner. This means that the launched wave has an electric and magnetic field relationship that is compatible with the natural guided surface wave mode supported at the interface between the lossy conducting medium and the surrounding dielectric, such as air. As a result, less energy is lost to radiation or inefficient coupling, and more of the applied energy is directed into the guided surface wave mode.

The use of the upper and lower terminal portions, together with adjustable capacitance and a properly tuned feed network, allows the probe to be adapted to different operating frequencies, medium conductivities, dielectric constants, and environmental conditions. Because real-world lossy conducting media may vary significantly in composition and electrical properties, the ability to tune the system is important for maintaining efficient operation. The probe may therefore be adjusted so that the launched wave remains substantially phase-matched to the desired surface wave mode even when the electrical properties of the medium change.

In operation, energy from a source is supplied to the feed network, which conditions the energy and applies it to the elevated charge terminal. The electric field established between the terminal structure and the lossy conducting medium creates surface-bound electromagnetic fields. When the terminal geometry, capacitance, and feed network parameters are properly selected, these fields couple strongly into a guided surface wave that travels along the interface of the lossy conducting medium rather than radiating primarily into free space.

This configuration improves coupling efficiency and supports longer-distance propagation of guided surface waves along the surface of the medium. By reducing mismatch losses and aligning the excitation fields with the medium’s complex Brewster angle, the enhanced guided surface waveguide probe provides a more effective mechanism for transferring electromagnetic energy over or along lossy conducting surfaces. Such systems may be useful in applications involving surface-wave communications, energy transfer, sensing, geophysical exploration, or other technologies that rely on controlled propagation of electromagnetic waves along conductive or partially conductive media.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize an invention for a guided surface waveguide probe system and method where an elevated charge terminal is fed with a phase delay matching the wave tilt angle associated with a lossy conducting medium.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention describes a guided surface waveguide probe system and method for launching and sustaining electromagnetic surface waves along a lossy conducting medium, such as the Earth.

The system uses an elevated charge terminal positioned above the conducting surface and energized by a source through a feed network. The feed network is configured so that the voltage or current applied to the elevated terminal has a phase delay selected to correspond to the wave tilt angle associated with the lossy conducting medium. This wave tilt angle reflects the relationship between the electric and magnetic field components of a surface-guided wave propagating along the interface between air and the lossy conductor.

By matching the phase delay of the terminal excitation to this wave tilt condition, the probe more efficiently couples energy into a guided surface wave mode rather than radiating energy as conventional space waves. The resulting electromagnetic wave is bound to, and propagates along, the surface of the conducting medium with reduced radiation loss.

The method includes determining electrical characteristics of the lossy conducting medium, calculating or otherwise identifying the associated wave tilt angle, positioning an elevated charge terminal at an appropriate height, and feeding the terminal with an excitation signal having the corresponding phase delay. The arrangement may also include impedance matching, resonant tuning, and compensation networks to improve coupling efficiency.

In essence, the invention provides a way to excite guided surface electromagnetic waves by synchronizing the phase of an elevated terminal’s excitation with the natural surface-wave field geometry of a lossy conductive medium.

A method and apparatus are provided for coupling electromagnetic energy into or from a lossy conducting medium. The apparatus includes a charge terminal positioned at a selected height above the medium and coupled to a feed network configured to excite the terminal with a controlled phase relationship. The medium is characterized by a complex permittivity, or equivalently by conductivity and dielectric constant, from which a complex Brewster angle of incidence is determined for a desired operating frequency. The feed network includes an adjustable phase-delay element configured to establish an effective incidence condition corresponding to the complex Brewster angle, thereby reducing reflected energy at the interface between the region containing the charge terminal and the lossy conducting medium.

In operation, the charge terminal is energized to produce an electromagnetic field having a vertical electric-field component directed toward the medium. A controller, tuning circuit, or manually adjustable network varies the phase delay between terminal excitation and a reference potential, counterpoise, ground structure, or auxiliary radiating element so that the launched field approximates the complex Brewster-angle condition. The adjustment may be based on measured impedance, reflected power, field strength, received signal level, or calculated medium parameters. By matching the phase delay to the complex Brewster angle, the system preferentially excites a surface or subsurface propagating mode while suppressing undesired reflection and radiation loss.

The disclosed technique is applicable to communication, sensing, geophysical probing, power transfer, and ground-wave or surface-wave launching systems operating over soil, seawater, brine, ore bodies, biological tissue, or other lossy conducting media. The apparatus may include variable reactance elements, transmission-line sections, phase shifters, impedance-matching components, sensors, and feedback control circuitry to maintain the Brewster-angle match as frequency or medium properties vary.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create patent-application language for a guided surface waveguide probe having an upper terminal portion coupled to a lower terminal portion through variable capacitance, with an excitation source coupled by a feed network providing phase-delayed voltage.
counterfactuals.output:
## Example Patent-Application Language

### Abstract

A guided surface waveguide probe includes an upper terminal portion and a lower terminal portion separated by a variable capacitance. An excitation source is coupled to at least one of the terminal portions through a feed network configured to provide a phase-delayed voltage to the probe. The variable capacitance is adjustable to tune an electrical relationship between the upper and lower terminal portions, thereby facilitating excitation of a guided surface wave along a terrestrial or other lossy conducting medium. The feed network may include one or more reactive, transmission-line, transformer, or phase-shifting elements arranged to establish a desired phase relationship between an excitation voltage and a current or voltage associated with the probe.

---

### Field

The present disclosure relates generally to electromagnetic wave propagation structures and, more particularly, to guided surface waveguide probes configured to launch, sustain, or receive guided surface waves along or adjacent to a lossy conducting surface, such as the surface of the Earth.

---

### Background

Electromagnetic energy may be transmitted through free space, through conductors, or along interfaces between materials having different electrical properties. In certain applications, it is desirable to excite a guided surface wave that propagates along a surface or interface, such as the interface between air and a terrestrial medium. Efficient excitation of such a guided surface wave may depend on the electrical configuration, geometry, and phase relationships of the excitation structure.

Conventional antenna structures may radiate a substantial portion of supplied energy into space rather than coupling energy into a guided surface mode. Accordingly, there exists a need for a guided surface waveguide probe having adjustable electrical characteristics to improve or control coupling to a guided surface wave mode.

---

### Summary

In one embodiment, a guided surface waveguide probe comprises a lower terminal portion, an upper terminal portion, and a variable capacitance coupled between the upper terminal portion and the lower terminal portion. An excitation source is coupled to the guided surface waveguide probe through a feed network. The feed network is configured to provide a phase-delayed voltage to at least one of the upper terminal portion or the lower terminal portion.

In another embodiment, the variable capacitance is adjustable to tune a phase relationship, voltage distribution, current distribution, effective electrical height, or resonant condition of the guided surface waveguide probe. The feed network may be configured to delay a voltage supplied by the excitation source relative to a reference voltage, current, ground potential, or another signal applied to the guided surface waveguide probe.

In some embodiments, the lower terminal portion is positioned closer to a terrestrial medium than the upper terminal portion. The lower terminal portion may be elevated above, capacitively coupled to, conductively coupled to, or otherwise referenced to the terrestrial medium. The upper terminal portion may be vertically spaced from the lower terminal portion and may comprise a conductive body, plate, sphere, toroid, cage, wire structure, or other terminal structure.

In some embodiments, the variable capacitance comprises an adjustable capacitor, a vacuum variable capacitor, a motor-driven capacitor, a switched capacitor bank, a varactor arrangement, a mechanically adjustable plate structure, or a combination thereof. The variable capacitance may be controlled manually or by a controller responsive to one or more sensed operating parameters.

In some embodiments, the feed network comprises a phase-delay network, impedance-matching network, resonant network, transmission-line section, transformer, inductive element, capacitive element, or any combination thereof. The feed network may be configured to provide a voltage to the probe having a predetermined phase delay selected to enhance coupling of energy into a guided surface wave.

---

### Detailed Description

A guided surface waveguide probe may include a plurality of conductive terminal portions arranged in a vertically distributed configuration. In an example embodiment, the probe includes an upper terminal portion disposed above a lower terminal portion. The upper and lower terminal portions are electrically coupled through a variable capacitance. The variable capacitance provides a controllable reactive coupling between the terminal portions and enables tuning of the guided surface waveguide probe for a selected operating frequency, environmental condition, surface conductivity, or load condition.

The lower terminal portion may be disposed at a height above a lossy conducting medium, such as the Earth. In other embodiments, the lower terminal portion may be positioned proximate to, embedded in, or electrically coupled with a ground reference, counterpoise, radial conductor system, ground screen, or other reference structure. The upper terminal portion may be supported by an insulating mast, tower, dielectric support, guyed structure, or other mechanical support.

An excitation source provides radio-frequency, alternating-current, pulsed, or time-varying electrical energy. The excitation source is coupled to the guided surface waveguide probe through a feed network. The feed network is arranged to provide a phase-delayed voltage to the probe. In one implementation, the phase-delayed voltage is applied to the lower terminal portion. In another implementation, the phase-delayed voltage is applied to the upper terminal portion. In still another implementation, different voltages having selected relative phase relationships are applied to the upper and lower terminal portions.

The phase delay may be selected such that the voltage at a terminal portion lags a source voltage, a feed-point current, a current in the lower terminal portion, a current in a ground-referenced conductor, or another electrical quantity by a predetermined phase angle. The phase angle may be selected based on an operating frequency, physical height of the probe, effective electrical length of the terminal portions, capacitance between the terminal portions, and electrical characteristics of the surface along which the guided surface wave is to propagate.

The variable capacitance between the upper terminal portion and the lower terminal portion may be adjusted to control the relative voltage amplitudes and phases appearing on the terminal portions. By controlling the variable capacitance and the feed-network phase delay, the probe may be tuned to establish a desired charge distribution on the terminal portions. The resulting electromagnetic fields may be configured to couple preferentially into a guided surface wave mode rather than into a radiation mode.

A controller may be provided to adjust the variable capacitance and/or one or more components of the feed network. The controller may receive feedback from voltage sensors, current sensors, phase detectors, field probes, power meters, reflected-power sensors, environmental sensors, or receivers positioned at one or more locations. Based on the feedback, the controller may tune the variable capacitance or phase delay to maintain a desired operating condition.

In some embodiments, the feed network includes an impedance transformation portion and a phase delay portion. The impedance transformation portion may match an output impedance of the excitation source to an input impedance associated with the guided surface waveguide probe. The phase delay portion may include one or more lumped reactive components or distributed transmission-line sections configured to introduce a selected phase shift at the operating frequency.

The guided surface waveguide probe may be used as a transmitting probe, a receiving probe, or a bidirectional transceiving probe. When operated in a receiving mode, a guided surface wave incident upon the probe induces electrical signals on the upper and lower terminal portions. The variable capacitance and feed network may be adjusted to improve reception of the guided surface wave and delivery of received energy to a load or receiver.

---

## Example Claims

### Claim 1 — Independent Apparatus Claim

1. A guided surface waveguide probe comprising:  
   a lower terminal portion;  
   an upper terminal portion spaced apart from the lower terminal portion;  
   a variable capacitance electrically coupled between the upper terminal portion and the lower terminal portion; and  
   a feed network configured to couple an excitation source to at least one of the upper terminal portion or the lower terminal portion,  
   wherein the feed network is configured to provide a phase-delayed voltage to the guided surface waveguide probe.

### Claim 2

2. The guided surface waveguide probe of claim 1, wherein the phase-delayed voltage is phase delayed relative to an output voltage of the excitation source.

### Claim 3

3. The guided surface waveguide probe of claim 1, wherein the phase-delayed voltage is phase delayed relative to a current supplied by the excitation source.

### Claim 4

4. The guided surface waveguide probe of claim 1, wherein the variable capacitance is adjustable to tune a phase relationship between a voltage of the upper terminal portion and a voltage of the lower terminal portion.

### Claim 5

5. The guided surface waveguide probe of claim 1, wherein the variable capacitance comprises at least one of an adjustable capacitor, a vacuum variable capacitor, a switched capacitor bank, a varactor, or a mechanically adjustable capacitive structure.

### Claim 6

6. The guided surface waveguide probe of claim 1, wherein the feed network comprises a phase-shifting network including at least one reactive component.

### Claim 7

7. The guided surface waveguide probe of claim 1, wherein the feed network comprises a transmission-line section configured to provide a predetermined phase delay at an operating frequency.

### Claim 8

8. The guided surface waveguide probe of claim 1, wherein the feed network comprises an impedance matching network configured to match an output impedance of the excitation source to an input impedance of the guided surface waveguide probe.

### Claim 9

9. The guided surface waveguide probe of claim 1, wherein the lower terminal portion is disposed closer to a terrestrial medium than the upper terminal portion.

### Claim 10

10. The guided surface waveguide probe of claim 9, wherein the lower terminal portion is capacitively coupled to the terrestrial medium.

### Claim 11

11. The guided surface waveguide probe of claim 9, wherein the lower terminal portion is conductively coupled to a ground reference associated with the terrestrial medium.

### Claim 12

12. The guided surface waveguide probe of claim 1, wherein the upper terminal portion comprises a conductive terminal selected from a group consisting of a plate, toroid, sphere, cage, wire frame, and conductive mesh.

### Claim 13

### Claim 14

14. The guided surface waveguide probe of claim 13, wherein the controller is configured to adjust the variable capacitance based on at least one sensed parameter selected from voltage, current, phase, impedance, reflected power, field strength, or received signal level.

### Claim 15

15. The guided surface waveguide probe of claim 1, wherein the feed network is configured to establish a selected phase relationship between a voltage applied to the lower terminal portion and a voltage appearing on the upper terminal portion.

### Claim 16 — Independent System Claim

16. A guided surface wave transmission system comprising:  
   an excitation source;  
   a guided surface waveguide probe comprising an upper terminal portion and a lower terminal portion coupled through a variable capacitance; and  
   a feed network coupled between the excitation source and the guided surface waveguide probe,

### Claim 20 — Independent Method Claim

20. A method of operating a guided surface waveguide probe, the method comprising:  
   providing a guided surface waveguide probe having an upper terminal portion and a lower terminal portion coupled through a variable capacitance;  
   generating an excitation signal using an excitation source;  
   applying the excitation signal to a feed network;  
   producing, by the feed network, a phase-delayed voltage; and  
   applying the phase-delayed voltage to the guided surface waveguide probe to excite a guided surface wave along a surface.

### Claim 21

21. The method of claim 20, further comprising adjusting the variable capacitance to tune a phase relationship between the upper terminal portion and the lower terminal portion.

### Claim 22

22. The method of claim 20, further comprising adjusting the feed network to vary a phase delay of the phase-delayed voltage.

### Claim 23

23. The method of claim 20, further comprising sensing at least one operating parameter of the guided surface waveguide probe and adjusting the variable capacitance based on the sensed operating parameter.

### Claim 24

24. The method of claim 20, wherein applying the phase-delayed voltage comprises applying the phase-delayed voltage to the lower terminal portion.

### Claim 25

25. The method of claim 20, wherein applying the phase-delayed voltage comprises applying the phase-delayed voltage to the upper terminal portion.

---

### Additional Broadening Language

In various embodiments, the phase delay introduced by the feed network may be fixed, adjustable, continuously variable, discretely selectable, or dynamically controlled. The phase delay may be selected to compensate for a physical height of the probe, a propagation characteristic of the guided surface wave, an impedance presented by the variable capacitance, or a characteristic of the medium adjacent the probe.

The terminal portions need not be limited to any particular shape, and may include any conductive body or arrangement capable of supporting charge distribution suitable for coupling electromagnetic energy to or from a guided surface wave mode. The upper and lower terminal portions may be coaxially aligned, laterally offset, concentrically arranged, or otherwise positioned relative to one another.

The variable capacitance may be located physically between the upper and lower terminal portions, electrically between the upper and lower terminal portions, or both. In certain embodiments, the variable capacitance may include parasitic capacitance supplemented by an adjustable capacitive element.

The excitation source may include a radio-frequency generator, power amplifier, oscillator, inverter, resonant power supply, pulsed source, or other source of time-varying electrical energy. The excitation source may operate at a frequency selected based at least in part on the desired guided surface wave propagation characteristics.

---

### Optional Means-Plus-Function Style Claim Language

A guided surface waveguide probe comprising:  
means for forming a lower terminal;  
means for forming an upper terminal spaced from the lower terminal;  
means for variably capacitively coupling the upper terminal to the lower terminal; and  
means for feeding excitation energy to the guided surface waveguide probe with a phase-delayed voltage.

---

   a phase-delay feed network coupled to an excitation source and configured to energize at least one of the first conductive terminal or the second conductive terminal with a voltage having a selected phase delay,
